title: WORKSHEET 7 (Review)
subject: Present Simple and Present Continuous Tense
subjectVi: Ngữ pháp bài 7: Present Simple and Present Continuous Tense

sections.instruction: Make questions and answers. Use THE PRESENT CONTINUOUS. (Example: (she / work / in Peru / this year?) (No, she / study / in Mexico) → Is she working in Peru this year? No. She's studying in Mexico.)

questions.prompt: (you / study / English / at the moment?) (Yes, I / work / hard.)
acceptedAnswers: Are you studying English at the moment? Yes, I'm working hard.
Are you studying English at the moment? Yes, I am. I'm working hard.

questions.prompt: (they / listen / to the radio?) (No, they / play / CDs.)
acceptedAnswers: Are they listening to the radio? No, they're playing CDs.
Are they listening to the radio? No, they aren't. They're playing CDs.

questions.prompt: (Peter / wash / now?) (Yes, he / have / a bath.)
acceptedAnswers: Is Peter washing now? Yes, he's having a bath.
Is Peter washing now? Yes, he is. He's having a bath.

questions.prompt: (they / live / in Madrid / at the moment?) (Yes, they / learn / Spanish.)
acceptedAnswers: Are they living in Madrid at the moment? Yes, they're learning Spanish.
Are they living in Madrid at the moment? Yes, they are. They're learning Spanish.

questions.prompt: (David / sing / in a group / this year?) (No, he / work / in a restaurant.)
acceptedAnswers: Is David singing in a group this year? No, he's working in a restaurant.
Is David singing in a group this year? No, he isn't. He's working in a restaurant.

sections.instruction: Choose TRUE for a correct sentence and FALSE for a wrong sentence. (Example: She's liking pop music. → FALSE; He's learning German. → TRUE)

questions.prompt: They're enjoying the film. [gap]
We're loving ice-cream. [gap]
She's believing he's right. [gap]
John's thinking about my idea. [gap]
He's having lunch at the moment. [gap]
She's eating a banana. [gap]
I'm feeling sick. [gap]
“Huge” is meaning “very big”. [gap]
Mick is knowing Jane. [gap]
She's hating classical music. [gap]

sections.instruction: Complete this conversation. Use the verbs in brackets in the PRESENT CONTINUOUS. (Paul: Hi Steve! What are you doing?)

questions.prompt: Steve: [gap] (I / go) to the bank. What are you doing?
Paul: [gap] (I / shop).
[gap] (I / look) for a new tennis racquet.
[gap] (I / play) a lot of tennis at the moment, and I need a new racquet.
Steve: Where is Jackie? Do you know? Paul: Yes. She isn't in England at the moment. [gap] (She / work) in Germany for a month.
Steve: What [gap] (she / do) in Germany?
Paul: [gap] (She / sing) in a night-club.
Steve: Really? What about Fred and Sue? What [gap] (they / do)?
Paul: [gap] (They / study) for an exam. They're always in the library at the moment.
Steve: How is your sister? Is she all right? Paul: Yes, she's fine, but she's tired. [gap] (We / paint) the living-room. It's hard work.
Steve: Can I help you? Paul: No, it's OK. My father [gap] (help).

sections.instruction: This is Anna's first letter in English to David. There are some mistakes. Write the correct verb form in each gap; if Anna's verb form is already correct, write it again unchanged. (Example: “I'm having two sisters.” → I have two sisters.)

questions.prompt: “I live in a large flat in Rome.” → I [gap] in a large flat in Rome.
“We are getting up at seven o'clock every morning.” → We [gap] at seven o'clock every morning.
“We have coffee and a small breakfast.” → We [gap] coffee and a small breakfast.
“I leave the flat at eight and walk to the university.” → I [gap] the flat at eight and walk to the university.
“I am finishing classes at five every day.” → I [gap] classes at five every day.
“I arrive home at six.” → I [gap] home at six.
“This month I work very hard for my exams.” → This month I [gap] very hard for my exams.
“At the moment, I eat breakfast in the kitchen of our flat.” → At the moment, I [gap] breakfast in the kitchen of our flat.
“My mother drinks coffee.” → My mother [gap] coffee.
“My sisters are reading magazines.” → My sisters [gap] magazines.
“On Saturday afternoons I am playing tennis with my friends.” → On Saturday afternoons I [gap] tennis with my friends.
“Or I go to the cinema.” → Or I [gap] to the cinema.
“Sometimes I am watching American films on TV.” → Sometimes I [gap] American films on TV.
“But I'm not understanding the words!” → But I [gap] the words!
“Are you liking films?” → [gap] films?

sections.instruction: Write sentences. Use the PRESENT SIMPLE or the PRESENT CONTINUOUS. (Example: Usually she / work / at the office, but this week she / work / at home. → Usually she works at the office, but this week she's working at home.)

questions.prompt: You / not / eat / very much at the moment. Are you ill?
acceptedAnswers: You aren't eating very much at the moment. Are you ill?
You're not eating very much at the moment. Are you ill?

questions.prompt: She / know / three words in Italian!
acceptedAnswers: She knows three words in Italian!

questions.prompt: I / take / the bus to work this week, but usually I / walk
acceptedAnswers: I'm taking the bus to work this week, but usually I walk.
I'm taking the bus to work this week but usually I walk.

questions.prompt: I / study / Japanese this year. It's very difficult.
acceptedAnswers: I'm studying Japanese this year. It's very difficult.

questions.prompt: you / watch / the television at the moment?
acceptedAnswers: Are you watching the television at the moment?

questions.prompt: I / not / remember / the name of the hotel.
acceptedAnswers: I don't remember the name of the hotel.

questions.prompt: She / speak / three languages.
The sun / shine. It's a beautiful day!
acceptedAnswers: The sun is shining. It's a beautiful day!
